For two curve summands, their sum x and second power sum y give product (x²−y)/2 and discriminant Δ=2y−x²; the third power sum is forced by V. The ordered fiber is therefore 1+χ(Δ) on V, including characteristic 3. A curve-plus-line decomposition has one choice of curve parameter on T since t is recovered by t³/t² away from zero. Subtract the common origin before squaring the convolution: on L the only curve-curve point is zero, and the net count is q everywhere. On T away from L the two oriented mixed representations remain. The curve-curve candidate equation is (x−t)²(x+2t)=0. At x=t the two curve-curve pairs both involve the origin and are already among the mixed pairs. At x=−2t they are genuinely new exactly when this is a distinct root and Δ=−2t² is a square. Thus char 3 eliminates the separate root, not its square character. In tallying, subtract the supported intersections from the curve-curve histogram: its q discriminant-zero points lose only the origin; its q(q−1)/2 two-pair points lose (q−1)(1+ε_q). Add the counts on T and L to obtain the displayed histogram; summing counts and their squares gives the claimed sumset and energy. Additive-character orthogonality with the unnormalized transform yields exactly the factor q⁻³ in the fourth moment. The proof's line 79 literally says V∩T contains the distinct −2t point only in the square phase; that is true for T intersected with the supported curve-curve convolution, not for V∩T as a bare algebraic set (e.g. (3,1,1) over F₅).
